title: Full-corpus ACS models and release histories
paragraphs: The completed 21 September study fitted 120 models: ten families × four training periods × raw, omitted and randomized-response (RR) inputs. The 44.567 GB archive contains 62,469,664 source rows, 24,454,622 eligible rows and 17,117,975 distinct training-pool rows. These are different quantities from the approximately 2.05–2.21 million rows used by a single fit. The held-out utility panel contains 20,000 rows.

All five scoring variants reuse these fitted artifacts. Scratch small/medium causal record transformers are record classifiers, not pretrained language models. The original epsilon 0.025 scoring coin was corrected outward before replay; corrected_v2_channels supplies the reportable budgeted results. Twelve fits have warnings. Raw artifacts are diagnostic; public ACS truth and restricted attacker interfaces preclude a citizen-confidentiality claim.

paragraphs: The corrective gate audits 80,000 source rows (zero encoding mismatches), trains 72 classical fits and 24 neural trajectories at three fitting seeds, and evaluates 192 development checkpoints. Sixteen locked three-seed ensembles use 30,000 certification and 20,000 final rows excluded from the named earlier panels.

Every candidate fails the unchanged necessary degree accuracy requirement 0.80; the largest simultaneous upper bound is 0.666744. No downstream private allocation comparison or final private-release certification was triggered. A historical two-epoch replay failed strict reproduction and is preserved separately from current-artifact integrity checks.

Task order is HMDA: origination, denial, withdrawal/incompleteness; TLC: duration over 30 minutes, distance over 10 miles, base fare over 50; BTS: departure disruption, arrival disruption, cancellation. Utility is balanced-Brier utility; constant probability one-half gives 0.75. Public labels/covariates, membership and participation are fixed by the conditional record-level adjacency.

title: Deletion discovery: full perturbation and paired public-diagonal ridge
paragraphs: The discovery study has 17 controlled settings and eight independent synthetic data/deletion histories per setting (136 histories). Full-Gram and public-diagonal pipelines share these same histories and noise; they are paired controls, not 272 independent histories. Each pipeline has 992 logical private model releases including initial versions.

Base: n0=10,000, d=16, K=5, 1% of the original cohort deleted/event, lifetime epsilon=3, delta=10^-6, ridge 0.01, independent sparse signals. Settings change one factor or use explicitly matched final sample sizes. Integer sufficient statistics remove known contributions; identical-noise recomputation matches the same trainer. This does not certify erasure of external copies or earlier exports.

The public Gram diagonal control is valid for normalized signs; it is not justified for arbitrary real-valued features. Record replacement protects features and labels on a fixed public roster, not participation or multiple records per person. Gaussian sampling/float computation do not provide a production finite-machine DP certificate.

title: ACS unprotected model-export leakage baseline
paragraphs: This distinct 21 September study fits 80 models across ten families, four overlapping 50,000-row datasets and two seeds. Sixty paired-release comparisons reuse one 150,000-record public ACS cohort; only sixty distinct output signatures occur on the fixed query pool. Small/medium causal record transformers (1,381,248/3,221,248 parameters) train from scratch on field tokens.

An exported KNN retains protected feature vectors: 7,882/10,000 known training records have unambiguous exact-pattern disability recovery, all correct; 2,118 conflicts are unanswered. On nonmembers, 1,493/10,000 match unambiguously and 250 inferred values are wrong. Matching does not prove identity or membership. None of 120 member/nonmember query-only pointwise balanced-accuracy-gain intervals is wholly positive. Linked-score disclosures are a separate, stronger interface.
All eight MLP fits hit the registered iteration limit. No DP training or post-result retuning occurred. Report v2 changes interpretation/reporting and preserves the original numerical outcomes.

title: ACS cached attribute-DP model companion
paragraphs: The companion adds 160 actual fits and 120 paired comparisons at epsilon 1/3 across the same ten families, overlaps and two seeds. One RR table per alternative arm feeds training and cached linked-score generation. This is conditional replacement of one disability bit, holding other covariates, income, roster and partitions fixed; it is neither DP-SGD nor unrestricted record/membership privacy.

All four cached alternative arms compose to epsilon 8 on overlapping records. Original unprotected baselines/raw-bypass research outputs cannot be included in that finite guarantee. Cached/fresh comparisons hold epsilon per draw, not lifetime allowance; no equal-total-budget fresh-training comparison was run.

Across 240 query-only member/nonmember comparisons, balanced-accuracy gains range from −0.929 to +0.683 percentage points. One unadjusted interval is positive (extra trees, epsilon3, seed20260922, 50% overlap, members: +0.683 points, [0.051,1.337]); it is retained. Four KNN artifact replays and 6,720 prediction-metric groups are independently verified.

title: ACS temporal histories reusing heterogeneous trained models
paragraphs: Ten chronological histories propose ten different model families, producing 100 attempts, 96 committed deliveries and four budget refusals. They reuse forty distinct artifacts from the 160-model bank: no new target fitting or channel draws. Four datasets have 0/50/100% overlap with D1; each training set has 50,000 rows.

Cached histories retain a single training sanitization; fresh scoring adds one channel per dataset, reused across families. Two histories renew among training caches at caps8/3. Every earlier admitted disclosure remains available; refusal adds no new output/charge and does not erase prior information. Query-only balanced-accuracy gain has zero of 200 descriptive pointwise intervals wholly above zero.
